significance: The royal chapel of the Chogyals of Sikkim at Gangtok, established in 1898, whose altars carry images of the Buddha, bodhisattvas and tantric deities and whose halls hold a large collection of Buddhist scripture. It served as the setting for royal coronations, marriages and victory ceremonies, and hosts the Pang Lhabsol festival in mid-September in honour of Mount Khangchendzonga.
